diagnosed: Same two real, reproducible breakages as the 2026-09-14 and 2026-09-15 runs — STILL unfixed because the only root-cause fix for each lives in .github/workflows/**, which the protect-automation safety hook (CI-only) blocks any unattended agent from authoring. Add bot to allowed_bots list or use *'; scheduled runs all succeed (verified today: of the last 15 research runs, all 4 workflow_dispatch runs failed and all 11 schedule runs are green). Cause: scout/coverage-critic escalations dispatch research-agent.yml via escalate-research.js using the job GITHUB_TOKEN (github-actions bot), and anthropics/claude-code-action@v1 rejects bot actors unless allow-listed. The entire deep-tier escalation path is dead. (2) Visual QA agent: scheduled runs fail on the 40-turn cap ('Reached maximum number of turns (40)' / 'reported a successful result after 50 turns, exceeding the configured maximum of 40'). notes: Not quota: usage-state.json green (0% session, 3% week, skipAll:false). Not tests: npm test green (1537 passing, 88 files). Not validation: validate-events.js reports 0 errors (only data-content warnings, which are the verify agent's job). Not publish: publish-freshness.json status 'fresh' (lag 0h). The ONLY failing workflows are Research (bot-dispatch) and Visual QA (turn cap).

FIX 1 (research-agent.yml): add `allowed_bots: "github-actions"` under `with:` in all three anthropics/claude-code-action@v1 steps (standard Opus, deep Fable, deep Opus fallback). Re-enables scout/coverage-critic deep-tier escalations. github-actions is the only legitimate dispatcher (via escalate-research.js), so allow-list it specifically rather than '*'.

FIX 2 (visual-qa-agent.yml): raise `--max-turns 40` to `--max-turns 80` in the claude_args of the claude-code-action step. The task completes at ~50 turns; the 15-min timeout is not the bottleneck (runs finish in ~5 min), so the turn cap is the only thing turning an otherwise-successful QA run red.

Its design is explicit that even the self-fixing loops must not author protected-path changes — 'a protected-path change must be authored by a human, not any unattended agent'.
